implemented: P09.1 authenticated tenant-scoped agent directory projects durable onboarding registrations, capability claims, provider mode, qualification expiry and explicit unverified ENS/affiliation/research-dispatch status
P09.1 registration challenge now validates the pinned Agent Card against the official A2A 0.3.0 schema before accepting its endpoint or capability claim

P09.1 institutional onboarding API and worker can use a dedicated coordinator identity without enabling the H04 prototype network; API receives only the public key and the worker validates its separate private key against it. The duplicate H04 /v1/network/agents route was removed so the full-plan paginated directory owns the path.

P09.1 tenant-scoped GET /v1/network/agents/{agent_id} reads the current registration and qualification expiry while exposing public endpoint and signing metadata with research and ENS trust still disabled

P09.1 capability and endpoint reads project the current immutable registration binding and label self-declared claims, service qualification and research dispatch separately. PATCH /v1/network/agents/{agent_id} replaces the binding through the existing versioned onboarding flow, resetting it to draft so proof and qualification must be repeated.

P09.1 organization operators can request a dedicated check of the registered endpoint through POST /v1/network/agents/{agent_id}/endpoint-checks. It uses bounded public HTTPS egress, checks the card digest, URL, protocol and capability, and records the outcome for the checked binding after a version recheck.

P09.1 endpoint checks now return 202 and run in the onboarding worker. The GET job route exposes progress and the report. Pending requests for the same binding, version and endpoint coalesce. Other submissions are limited to one per registration per 60 seconds. The worker rechecks the actor's authority and binding before fetching and before recording the observation.

P09.1 versioned create and replace-registration APIs accept additional capabilities on the primary endpoint and additional HTTPS endpoints with their own pinned card digests and advertised capabilities. The directory can filter by any declared capability. Endpoint jobs can select only a URL in the current binding. Additional declarations remain unqualified until separately approved.

P09.1/P09.3 secondary endpoint qualification is a separate rate-limited onboarding job for the supported temperature_summary_v1 protocol. It proves the registered service key at the selected endpoint and records evidence for the exact binding, endpoint and capability. An explicit secondary dispatch additionally needs policy approval for that endpoint; the signed grant binds the endpoint through dispatch, cancellation and readback. Primary requests retain the legacy defaults.

Earlier H04/F02 work includes an official A2A 0.3.0 SDK client, provider servers, scoped signed requests, durable provider tasks and cancellation; these are reusable foundations for P09.2, not a P09 gate pass

P09.3 signed research-grant policy binds one agent and immutable binding to organization, project, run, task, approved plan/method, dataset allowlist, reserved-budget ceiling and a maximum five-minute lifetime; policy rejects research dispatch unless separately enabled

P09.2/P09.3 research A2A client now uses the official SDK with the existing pinned-public-HTTPS transport, checks the current provider binding, registered Agent Card digest, bearer request digest, completed task, provider-signed grant-bound artifact and task readback. This client is not yet wired to durable run jobs or enabled for production dispatch.

P09.3 durable remote-dispatch intents now reference the approved run, exact binding, current service qualification, project source grants, policy-only research authorization and a bounded share of the existing reserved run budget. Runtime cannot create research authorizations.

P09.3 separate worker claims intents with SKIP LOCKED and generation/token/expiry fences, persists a short-lived signed grant before the official A2A exchange, rechecks run reservation, project permission, source grants, binding, qualification and policy authorization before and after the call, and stores only a provider-signed artifact verified against the persisted grant. Expired leases and ambiguous remote failures require reconciliation instead of automatic replay. Transport completion does not imply a correct scientific result.

P09.3 run-scoped HTTP endpoints enqueue, inspect and cancel remote intents. Cancellation invalidates the local lease atomically, records whether a grant could have been sent, and retains the allocation when execution may have begun. Worker result writes use a database-time fence and the exchange has a 90 second timeout.

P09.2/P09.3 worker checkpoints the provider task and context, even when the local intent is cancelled during send. With a known task reference and a still valid grant, it reserves one provider cancellation attempt, uses official A2A tasks/get and tasks/cancel against the originally pinned binding, and exposes confirmation after matching status readback.

P09.3 operator worker command --reconcile reads a single uncertain dispatch with tasks/get. A 90-second research:readback credential binds the lookup to the original grant digest and task ID, even after execution-grant expiry. If the remote ID is missing, lookup uses the original grant task UUID and needs a provider that indexes the task under that ID. A completed signed response is persisted only after current authorization and dispatch state are rechecked. Missing or unverifiable outcomes remain unresolved.

P09.3 the institutional provider can opt into bounded, operator-approved temperature research tasks. It validates the coordinator grant against its pinned binding and exact plan, organization, project and dataset list. Signed artifacts are persisted before acknowledgment and readback accepts only tasks/get for the credential's task and grant digest. The original grant UUID resolves the same durable A2A task after restart.
P09.3 completing a dispatch or reconciliation now locks its active policy authorization and source grants through the result transaction. The runtime retains read-only policy access.

P09.4 tenant-scoped append-only dispatch history captures local run and agent binding, remote task and context, grant and result digests, state changes and cancellation observations. The events API pages by dispatch sequence. History begins when migration 0038 is applied.

P09.4 offline summary verifier checks coordinator and provider signatures, rechecks dataset IDs and input digest, and independently recomputes bounded Celsius/Kelvin arithmetic summaries in a separate process.
